The Mining Supervisor of the Geological Survey has the authority for the regulatory supervision of operations under Federal and Indian coal leases. He is empowered to regulate operations and to perform other duties prescribed in the regulations either personally or through subordinates acting under his direction. On Indian coal leases, if the Mining Supervisor determines there is noncompliance with the terms and conditions of a permit or lease, the Reservation Superintendent serves notice of noncompliance upon the operator.
Westmoreland Resources is required to submit plans for any mining or exploration activity on the leases to the Bureau of Indian Affairs and the Geological Survey for approval, and where applicable, to the appropriate agency of the State of Montana. These plans specify in detail:
(1) the placement of structures;
(2) mining procedures, sequences, and schedules; and
(3) methods of reclamation.
Compliance with the provisions of the lease and objectives of the mining plan are reviewed by periodic inspections of the Mining Supervisor, who then takes appropriate modification and/or enforcement measures. A key element in this process is a periodic review which evaluates the adequacy of the mining plan and the effectiveness of the methods as well as the degree of compliance. This process permits a flexibility and adaptability in the mining and reclamation operations
